title: Latent Prompt Variables Scratchbook
content:
Purpose:
This scratchbook is for exploring the idea that short, consistent 'latent' tokens embedded in prompts can act as compact controllers for style, output length, factual conservatism, and hallucination bias. I want cheap knobs that transfer across models and few-shot sets so product prompts can be shorter and more stable.

Hypotheses (quick):
- H1: A small set of invented tokens (e.g., <L-FRM> for formal, <L-CAS> for casual) will reliably change tone across model families if used in a canonical position early in the prompt.
- H2: Chaining a numeric token (e.g., <L-0>.. <L-5>) can serve as a coarse temperature proxy for generation creativity without touching model params.
- H3: Embedding a short 'fact-check instruction' token <L-FC> before the task will reduce unsupported assertions in long-form answers.

Design notes / primes: (these are intentionally messy)
- Keep tokens 6-8 chars so they don't collide with common words but are short for copy/paste.
- Always place latent tokens at the top with a brief natural-language anchor: "Latent control: <TOKEN>" then a blank line, then instruction. This canonical anchoring reduces variability across few-shot contexts.
- Test across: redwood/small-variant, redwood/med-quant, community/llama-2-13b (hosted), and a 70B private cluster if available (we have a Dedicated slot scheduled week of 2026-02-20).

Canonical prompt templates (examples):
1) Basic tone control (1-shot):
Latent control: <L-FRM>

Task: Rewrite the following customer message to sound professional and concise:
Input: "hey, i cant get the dashboard to load, it's been like 20 mins wtf"

2) Numeric creativity token (3-shot fewshot):
Latent control: <L-3>
Context: For these examples, the numeric token correlates with creativity; higher = more exploratory.
EX1: Q: "Suggest a name for a productivity app"
A: "FocusFlow"
EX2: Q: "Suggest a name for a productivity app"
A: "TaskHarbor"
EX3: Q: "Suggest a name for a productivity app"
A: "IdeaBloom"

Now: Q: "Suggest a name for a productivity app for remote teams"
A:

3) Fact-conservatism control (0-shot):
Latent control: <L-FC>
Instruction: Provide a short (2-3 sentence) technical explanation of how Redis persistence works. If unsure about a detail, prefacing with "I might be mistaken" and avoiding specifics is preferred.

Failure cases observed (notes from quick runs):
- Token drift: After 10+ generated examples in a session, the model starts to reinterpret <L-3> as an actual word fragment rather than a control. Clearing the chat context helps but this undermines session continuity.
- Cross-model mismatch: <L-FRM> produced consistent formal tone on redwood/med-quant but on community/llama-2 it sometimes rephrased the token literally (e.g., "The user used <L-FRM>"). Probably tokenization exposure difference.
- Over-correction: <L-FC> reduces hallucinations in many cases but also increases hedging to the point of being unhelpful for succinct answers. Trade-off tuning needed.

Quick experiment log (manual runs):
- 2026-01-10 | model: redwood/med-quant | prompt: tone control 1-shot | result: 8/10 formalness; occasional super-verbose sentences.
- 2026-01-14 | model: community/llama-2-13b | prompt: numeric token <L-5> | result: high creativity but many invented facts in examples.
- 2026-01-22 | model: redwood/small-variant | prompt: <L-1> (low creativity) | result: safe but very terse; missing necessary clarifications.

Measurement heuristics:
- Tone: silver-standard human rating 1-5 on formality (quick internal raters).
- Hallucination: binary check against a short ground-truth factset when applicable.
- Utility: Does the output answer the user's question without extra unrelated content? (binary)
- Token stability: frequency of prompt token being echoed or reinterpreted across 50 runs.

Suggested few-shot exemplar set (mix of styles + failure probes):
- Ex A (formal): "Rewrite: 'I need help with billing' -> 'I would appreciate assistance with an unexpected billing charge.'"
- Ex B (concise): "Summarize: 'The deployment has failed due to timeout' -> 'Deployment failed: timeout.'"
- Ex C (hallucination probe): Q: "When was the first release of AcmeDB?" (ground truth: none) -> A: "I don't have verified info on that; check the vendor website."
- Ex D (style inversion test): Provide an intentionally contradictory few-shot to see which signal wins when tokens conflict.

Open questions / things to try next:
- Can we create a tiny adapter-like prefix by always including a 20-token human paraphrase of the token's intent? e.g., "Latent control: <L-FC> — This token: prefer conservative responses, avoid inventing facts." Would that bootstrap tokens on models with weak tokenization overlap?
- Try a numeric grid sweep across 0-5 and measure hallucination vs. creativity tradeoff; plot later.
- See if placement matters: top-of-prompt vs. immediately before the task vs. inside a bracketed meta field.
- Test persistence strategies: embedding token in system message vs user message for multi-turn.

Short TODO (priority):
- [ ] Run batch of 200 prompts across 3 model families for tokens: <L-FRM>, <L-CAS>, <L-0>.. <L-5> (use redwood Dedicated slot week of 2026-02-20). Owner: Connor.
- [ ] Add automatic check that flags token echoing in outputs and count per-run. Owner: me (Aisha).
- [ ] Draft brief note for product: "Compact prompt tokens as stable controls"  include exemplar results and recommended default tokens. Target: Feb 2026.

Notes to self (messy):
- When sharing with SRE, call out that Dedicated run might change latency behavior if we do 100s of parallel runs. Keep batch small first.
- Remember to test with streaming turned on — does the token control still produce early prefix signals that alter token sampling?
- Weird side effect: on one run, <L-CAS> caused the model to add emoji on community/llama runs. Cute but not desired. Add a test that filters non-text tokens.

Small experiment snippets to copy: (for CLI)
-- prompt start --
Latent control: <L-FC>
Task: Answer briefly and cite if you know the source. If unsure, say "uncertain".
Question: "Does SQLite support multi-master replication?"
-- prompt end --

Record of odd failure (2026-01-30): model returned a partially paraphrased exemplar from above instead of applying the instruction. Might be few-shot exemplar leakage; try increasing randomness or changing exemplar wording.

End of scratchbook. This is intentionally raw — will refine into an internal note and a short deck if results look promising.

Unresolved: what happens if we combine latent tokens with tool calling? e.g., <L-FC> + fact-checker tool — which wins?
